edges.description: Reduced amount and function of the synthetase lowers the supply of charged mitochondrial threonyl-tRNA.
Variants in the residue 301 to 381 region reduce binding to Rag GTPases, which is a separate consequence from any effect on aminoacylation.
edges.target: Reduced Rag GTPase Binding and mTORC1 Dysregulation

edges.description: Mitochondrial translation cannot proceed without an adequate supply of the charged tRNA for every amino acid.
Insufficient synthesis of the mitochondrially encoded subunits leaves the complexes that contain them unable to assemble and remain stable.
Deficient respiratory complexes cannot sustain electron transport and proton pumping, so ATP output falls and pyruvate is diverted to lactate.

edges.description: Energy failure in the developing brain, and particularly in the cerebellum and basal ganglia, produces the developmental, cerebellar and extrapyramidal phenotype.

edges.description: Proposed as a route to the neurodevelopmental phenotype independent of the respiratory chain defect, acting through neuronal proliferation and apoptosis. The intermediates between mTORC1 dysregulation and the human brain phenotype are not established, hence the indirect link type.

edges.description: The most striking prediction of this arm, because it explains a phenotype the translational model does not. One Rag-binding-region variant, p.(Arg327Gln), was found homozygously in four individuals with neonatal diabetes, and mTORC1 is essential to beta cells.
edges.source: Reduced Rag GTPase Binding and mTORC1 Dysregulation

edges.description: Beta cell failure presents clinically as insulin-treated diabetes, diagnosed within the first week of life in three of the four reported individuals.
Progressive loss of cerebellar, basal ganglia and white matter tissue produces the developmental, cerebellar and extrapyramidal deficits.

Morphants show reduced head size, a smaller cerebellum, extensive brain apoptosis, reduced myelination and increased seizure-associated gene expression, which map onto the human microcephaly, cerebellar atrophy, white matter change and epilepsy. It is partial rather than full recapitulation because the model produces developmental hypoplasia in an embryo rather than the progressive postnatal atrophy that characterises the human disease, and because heart edema is a morphant phenotype without a direct human counterpart.
edges.limitations: Morpholino knockdown is a transient, dose-dependent reduction rather than a model of the human hypomorphic missense alleles, and morpholinos are known to produce off-target phenotypes. The rescue experiments control for that but do not make the knockdown a genetic model of the disease. The readouts are embryonic, so nothing in this model speaks to the progressive postnatal course.

edges.description: The model provides the only in vivo readout of the mTORC1 arm, through two transcriptional targets of the pathway moving in the expected directions.
edges.limitations: Fidelity is LOW because a knockdown removes the protein entirely and therefore cannot distinguish the Rag-binding defect specific to the residue 301 to 381 variants from the general consequence of losing the synthetase. mTORC1 activity itself is not measured; the readout is the expression of two downstream targets.

nodes.description: Symptomatic, and the only pharmacological intervention with reported outcomes in this disorder. Seizures occurred in eight individuals in the largest cohort and were successfully controlled in half of them, so the response is real but partial. No agent is established as preferable, and no disease-modifying therapy exists.

nodes.description: The defining biochemical lesion, and the one the disease is named for. Complexes I, III, IV and V are deficient together because each contains mitochondrially encoded subunits; complex II is normal because it does not. Two practical qualifications attach to it. The defect is tissue-restricted and is found in muscle rather than reliably in fibroblasts or liver, so a normal fibroblast enzymology does not exclude the diagnosis. And it is inconsistently found even when looked for: of two patients biopsied in the largest cohort, one showed complex I deficiency and the other did not, so modern diagnosis rests on sequencing rather than on enzymology.

nodes.description: The clinical endpoint. Almost all patients have moderate or severe developmental delay or intellectual disability, and about a third lose acquired milestones, typically triggered by an intercurrent illness and often within the first year of life. That regression pattern is what marks the disorder as metabolic rather than statically developmental, and it is curated as its own node rather than folded into the structural one because the two are measured differently and can diverge: a child can regress after an illness without a new imaging finding.

nodes.description: Charging mitochondrial tRNA-Thr with threonine is the enzyme's canonical job, and it has a second, quality-control half: clearing mischarged seryl-tRNA-Thr through the editing domain. Both matter, since disease alleles fall in the editing domain as well as the catalytic one. Measured threonyl-tRNA levels are reduced in patient samples in proportion to the genetic defect.

nodes.description: Mitochondria translate only thirteen proteins, all of them subunits of the respiratory chain, but they need a full translation apparatus to do it: two ribosomal RNAs and twenty-two transfer RNAs encoded by mitochondrial DNA, plus more than a hundred nuclear-encoded proteins imported from the cytosol. The aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases are among those imported proteins, which is why a nuclear gene defect produces what looks like a mitochondrial DNA disease.

evidence.reference_title: VARS2 and TARS2 mutations in patients with mitochondrial encephalomyopathies.
evidence.snippet: Translation of the 13 mtDNA-encoded, OXPHOS-related proteins takes place within the mitochondrial matrix. This complex process requires ribosomal and transfer RNAs (rRNAs and tRNAs), encoded by mtDNA, and more than 100 proteins, encoded by nuclear genes, translated by cytosolic ribosomes and imported into mitochondria.

nodes.description: Falling ATP output from oxidative phosphorylation forces reliance on glycolysis, and the resulting raised blood lactate is the most consistent laboratory abnormality in the disorder, present in 85 percent of those tested. Lactate can also be seen directly in the brain: magnetic resonance spectroscopy has shown a lactate peak at the basal ganglia in a patient whose imaging lesions were progressing there.

nodes.description: Genotype-restricted rather than general. Four individuals homozygous for p.(Arg327Gln), one of the Rag GTPase-binding-region variants, presented with insulin-treated diabetes, three of them within the first week of life and the fourth at one year. nodes.description:
The structural consequence, and the point at which the two mechanistic arms converge on tissue. Imaging shows cerebellar atrophy with a vermian predominance in three quarters of patients, basal ganglia signal change in about two thirds, and progressive loss of periventricular white matter with callosal thinning in over 40 percent.
Two temporal points matter for diagnosis. The cerebellum was normal in one infant imaged in the first months of life, so a normal early MRI does not exclude the disorder and follow-up imaging is needed. And in at least two patients the basal ganglia lesions progressed with lactate peaks and new dentate signal change, producing a Leigh-like pattern.

nodes.description:
The non-translational arm. mTORC1 is recruited to and activated at the lysosomal surface by Rag GTPases in response to amino acid availability, and TARS2 is part of how threonine availability is read: on threonine supplementation it binds RagC preferentially and drives the conversion of the Rag heterodimer to its active form. The region responsible, residues 301 to 381, sits between the editing and catalytic core domains, and four disease variants fall inside it. All four bound RagA and RagC significantly less than wild type.
The confidence is PROVISIONAL and the limitations are specific. The transfected variant constructs also had reduced basal expression, between 39 and 66 percent of wild type, which the authors attribute to intrinsic instability, so reduced binding cannot be entirely separated from reduced protein. mTORC1 activity itself was not measured in patient cells. What is measured downstream comes from the zebrafish knockdown, where two mTORC1 targets move in opposite directions as expected.

nodes.description:
TARS2 encodes a 718-residue mitochondrial threonyl-tRNA synthetase with four domains: an N1 domain, an editing domain that clears mischarged seryl-tRNA-Thr, an aminoacylation domain, and an anticodon-binding domain. Disease variants are predominantly missense and cluster in three places: the Rag GTPase-binding region between the editing and catalytic core domains, the editing domain, and the anticodon-binding domain. Recurrent alleles are common, including p.(Thr157Arg), which recurs in Chinese families and is absent from other populations, and p.(Pro155Leu), p.(Glu512Lys) and p.(Ser258Leu), each seen in more than one unrelated family.
Which domain an allele hits matters. Variants in the Rag-binding region behave differently from the rest, both in the laboratory and in the clinic, and are the basis of the second mechanistic hypothesis curated here.

nodes.description: A morpholino knockdown of tars2 in zebrafish embryos, validated by rescue with either zebrafish tars2 or human TARS2 messenger RNA, which is what establishes that the phenotypes are specific to loss of Tars2 and that the function is conserved. The model was then used as an assay: seventeen human variants were tested for their ability to rescue, and none rescued fully.
